chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskhan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who invests in crops, takes some of the produce, and the remainder is insufficient to repay the principal, so he returns the principal to his partner. He said: 'Let him take it, for it is permissible.' I said: 'He sells what he has taken from the produce to double it.' He said: 'Even if he does, it is permissible.' And I asked him about a man who invests in something other than crops or date palms. He said: 'He specifies an amount for a specified period.'

key_terms.يُسْلِمُ: to invest or deposit capital in a partnership

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on keeping insufficient produce as a partner's share in an agricultural investment?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses the permissibility of *mudarabah* (profit-sharing partnership) in agriculture and general trade, specifically clarifying that retaining a share of produce insufficient to cover the principal remains lawful. It further permits reinvesting or doubling the capital through the sale of the produce, and establishes the mechanism for fixed-term investments in non-agricultural assets by specifying the amount and duration. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Shia commercial jurisprudence in accommodating practical economic arrangements while ensuring contractual clarity.
